resources.string: Larger bubble text during a shift
Choose which delivery apps gig.log reads. Shift tracking works only in apps gig.log fully supports.

Saves your full history as spreadsheet files in a folder you choose:
deliveries.csv: one row per delivery
sessions.csv: one row per shift
summary.csv: totals and estimated IRS mileage deduction
expenses.csv: logged expenses, including undone ones
fuel.csv: logged fill-ups, including undone ones

The files include store names, your expense labels as you typed them and gig.log's tracked miles at each fill-up. Customer names and addresses, which gig.log keeps only as codes, are left out. gig.log doesn't upload them, but a cloud folder may. The files stay after you uninstall; delete them from the folder. Exporting again replaces them.
Exported %1$d files to the chosen folder.
Export failed (%1$s). Check the folder and try again.

Saves a bug report, giglog-bug-report.txt, to a folder you choose. It lists the app\'s main events, like offers and deliveries. gig.log replaces known private details first but can miss some, so read it before sharing. gig.log doesn\'t send it to the developer; a cloud folder may upload it. It stays after uninstall; delete it from the folder. Exporting again replaces it.
Exported giglog-bug-report.txt. Private details removed from %1$d lines.
Bug report export failed (%1$s). Check the folder and try again.
Each automatic tap stays off until you allow it, and gig.log asks again when its instructions for finding that button change. Your own Accept and Decline presses work either way.
No automatic taps yet. They show up when a delivery app supports them.
When %1$s asks you to confirm a decline, gig.log taps Decline again for you, after checking the label. Works only with Quick declines on in Offer rules.
Not used yet. gig.log has no automatic accept or decline, so this choice changes nothing today.
After a %1$s delivery, gig.log taps the arrow that opens the pay details, so it can record them. The arrow has no label, so gig.log checks only that it is in %1$s.
Offers carry a Protect acceptance rate note. Nothing is tapped for you.
When off, shopping offers carry a Shopping off note. Nothing is tapped for you.
After you tap Decline, gig.log taps the confirm button. Needs your OK under Automation & Consent.
Drag to reorder. Rules higher up count more.

Off unless you turn it on. A screenshot is saved only when this switch and its type below are on; the types start on.

A screenshot shows the whole screen, including customer details, other apps and anything else showing, like a video or the keyboard. It goes to Pictures/gig.log. gig.log never uploads it, but gallery sync or sharing can. Screenshots stay after you uninstall; delete them in your gallery.

None is taken if this switch is off or another app is in front at that moment; one already saving still finishes. This switch doesn't affect your shift history.
Which app the bubble shows when two delivery apps are online. In every mode, cards and the chat header name their app.
Shows the delivery app you used last. A pick in the bubble\'s switcher holds until that app\'s shift ends, then the bubble follows again.
Your switcher pick stays until you change it, even across that app\'s next shift. While that app is offline, the bubble shows the app you used last.
Test mode: one stack of cards from every app with a live shift, each labeled with its app. No switcher; the chat follows the app you used last.
Optional. gig.log still works without it, using screen changes from the delivery apps only.

gig.log gets a signal from every app when its screen changes. It reads and saves screens only from the delivery apps you turn on; of other apps it sees only the name. Screenshots, if you turn them on, save the whole screen, including any app behind an offer.
Lets gig.log catch an offer that pops up over another app.
In this test build, screen reading turns itself off and the app can\'t be used until you allow them again.
On Android 11, this may not take effect.
See which other app is open

Forgets this phone\'s census install ID and secret, deletes the waiting outlines and captures, and turns capture sharing off. The next upload signs up a new install ID, which the census server must trust again. The Census upload switch stays as it is.

Sends the text of screens gig.log doesn\'t recognize to the census server while the server trusts this install. These screens get only the general privacy filters, so a capture can still hold customer details that the server\'s operator can read.
Highlights the bubble\'s Odometer button early in a shift, and after one until you log a reading

Screens of the delivery apps you turn on, through Android Accessibility, and with Screen events on, the name of the app in front. Those apps\' notifications; other apps\' are skipped unread. GPS during a shift. Gas-price lookups use your last location each time they run (daily when automatic, in setup for each fuel type while automatic updates are on, and when you refresh it or choose Use auto price in the bubble), even off shift. Screen reading and calculations happen on your phone. Recognized banking, payment and ID screens, the ID camera and the signature pad are dropped unsaved. The filters work in English and can miss a screen.

Customer names and addresses in your history are saved as codes, so gig.log can tell customers apart without knowing who they are. Store names and addresses are saved as text. Screenshots are pictures and keep everything on screen.

From the screens and notifications it recognizes: shifts, offers, deliveries and pay. From what you enter: expenses, fill-ups, cash tips, notes, odometer readings, vehicles, your goal and settings. Also the miles GPS counted, and a log of main events that keeps only recent entries.

gig.log has no account and no ads ID, and includes no outside analytics code. Gas-price lookups: Android\'s address lookup may send your last location to its provider to find your region, and the U.S. Energy Information Administration gets a price request for that region, with no account or install ID. Daily updates are off on a new install, and an update keeps your setting; to stop them, set the bubble\'s gas price to manual, or turn off daily updates in setup and save. Vehicle lookup starts after you tap \"Look up my vehicle\". gig.log saves that choice. The year, make, model and EPA vehicle ID you pick go to fueleconomy.gov, with no account or install ID. \"Search Google for MPG\" opens Google with the year, make and model. Spoken offers go to your phone\'s text-to-speech engine, which may use the network. Exports go to the folder you choose, and a cloud folder may upload them; spreadsheets leave out customer codes, and bug reports replace known private details but can miss some.

Off unless turned on in Settings > Data & privacy > Screenshots. A picture of the whole screen, including customer details and any app behind an offer, saved to Pictures/gig.log. gig.log never uploads it; gallery sync or sharing can. It stays after uninstall until you delete it.
Android backup and phone transfer may copy your history and settings and restore them. Consent choices and logs are left out, so a new phone asks again.

Until you clear app data or uninstall, though a backup can bring it back on a reinstall or a new phone. Logs keep only recent entries. Screenshots and exports stay until you delete them. There is no one-tap delete yet.

Each choice on Automation & consent is saved on this phone with its date, app version and privacy notice version. The app log notes each automatic-tap choice and leaves the phone only in a bug report you export; the saved records are not exported.

This test build saves the text of the delivery apps\' screens and notifications on the phone. On screens it recognizes, its rules replace the customer details they know about; elsewhere the filters can miss them. Its log also keeps screen text. That text stays until removed or uninstalled, and backup and transfer leave it out. Census upload, off unless turned on in developer options, sends outlines of unrecognized screens and notifications, plus counts showing which screens gig.log recognizes and the app version, with this install\'s ID. Capture sharing, also off unless turned on, needs census upload and the server\'s trust; it sends the text of unrecognized screens, never notifications, and the server\'s operator can read it. Screen events are required: without them, screen reading turns itself off and the app can\'t be used.
